title: Birth in Atlanta, her father's name, and meeting him in 1952
summary: Born in Atlanta in 1910 as Mary Louise Scruggs, out of wedlock. She finally met her father in 1952 through her half-brother Willis; his first words were asking what she had brought him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let's start from the beginning. When were you born and where?
I was born in Atlanta, Georgia, 1910, 8th of May.
8th of May, 1910. What was your name when you were born?
Mary Louise Scruggs. That was my father's name. I was born out of wedlock.
Did you know your father?

I met my father. Before I went to Europe I had to go to Atlanta, Georgia, to find out my birth date, because it seems that during the period when I was born they had these - what do they call the women that delivered babies?
Midwives.
Midwives, and my mother didn't really remember my birth date. I couldn't get it in Pittsburgh so I had to go back to Atlanta, Georgia, to try to get it.
And you met your father there?
No. I met him in 1952.
How did you run into him then?
I have a half-brother in Atlanta, Georgia. He's a school teacher -
What's his name?
Willis Scruggs. He was just a little boy when I was about 2 or 3 years old. He just loved music arou
WILLIAMS

the house and he played and he's always had an admiration for my playing, to note that I had started so early. When I went to Atlanta, Georgia to try to get a birth certificate he took me out to meet my Dad.
You met him?
Yes, I met him.
How did you get along?

Well, the one thing that was a drag to me, he says, "You know who I am?" I said, "No." He said, "I'm your father. What'd you bring me?" I said, "Of all things, you've never done anything for me." So that ruined my day almost.
That was the end of your father as far as you were concerned. Did you know anything about his background at all?
